title_jp: どうして{信州|しんしゅう}はそばなの？
context: Wednesday 9 December: ハナおばあちゃん comes to the {田中|たなか} kitchen with buckwheat flour to make soba with {恵子|けいこ}さん. When アルちゃん asks why Nagano is famous for soba, she explains how rice was paid as tax in the Edo period.
scene: Wednesday evening. ハナおばあちゃん is making soba in the {田中|たなか} kitchen. You ask why Nagano is so famous for it.

phrases.jp: {寒い|さむい}から、お{米|こめ}があまり{育たなかった|そだたなかった|to grow (up)|4}んです。
phrases.en: Because it's cold, rice didn't grow well.
phrases.note: 〜から + 〜んです: giving a reason and explaining.

phrases.jp: {理由|りゆう|reason|4}はいくつかあります。
phrases.note: Start of any explanation: then 一つ{目|め}は… (the first is…).

phrases.jp: {当時|とうじ|those days, back then|3}の{政治|せいじ|politics, government|3}は{厳しかった|きびしかった}そうです。
phrases.en: They say the government back then was harsh.
phrases.note: {当時|とうじ}: talking about a past period, as in a museum.

phrases.jp: そばを{食べれば|たべれば}、{長生き|ながいき|long life|3}できるって。
phrases.en: They say if you eat soba, you live long.
phrases.note: 〜って at the end = I heard / people say (casual).
When a reason finally clicks. Polite: なるほど、だからですね。

dialogue_setting: The {田中|たなか} kitchen on a snowy Wednesday evening. ハナおばあちゃん rolls the dough; {恵子|けいこ}さん boils the water.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: ハナおばあちゃん、どうして{長野|ながの}はそばが{有名|ゆうめい|famous|4}なんですか。
dialogue.en: ハナおばあちゃん, why is Nagano famous for soba?

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: {山|やま}が{多くて|おおくて}{寒い|さむい}からじゃ。{米|こめ}が{よう||(old/regional) = よく, well|2}{育たん|そだたん|(old/regional) = 育たない, not grow|2}{土地|とち|land|3}でも、そばなら{育つ|そだつ|to grow (up)|4}んよ。
dialogue.en: Because it's mountainous and cold. Even on land where rice won't grow well, soba grows.
dialogue.note: じゃ = だ, よう{育|そだ}たん = よく{育|そだ}たない (old, regional).

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: それに{のう||(old) sentence ending = ね|1}、そばは{種|たね|seed|3}を{まけば||to sow (seeds)|3}、七十五{日|にち}で{食べられる|たべられる}んじゃ。
dialogue.en: And you know, if you sow soba seeds, you can eat it in 75 days.
dialogue.note: のう = ね, じゃ = だ (old). まく = to sow.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: え、じゃあ{昔|むかし}は、お{米|こめ}はあまり{食べなかった|たべなかった}んですか。
dialogue.en: Oh, so back then people didn't eat much rice?

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: {米|こめ}は{年貢|ねんぐ|rice tax (Edo period)|2}として{殿様|とのさま}に{納めた|おさめた|to pay (tax)|2}。{納めなければ|おさめなければ|to pay (tax)|2}、{罰|ばつ}じゃった。
dialogue.en: Rice was paid to the lord as tax. If you didn't pay, you were punished.
dialogue.note: じゃった = だった (old). {年貢|ねんぐ} = rice tax farmers paid in the Edo period.

dialogue.speaker: 恵子さん
dialogue.jp: だから{隼人|はやと}さまも、そばが{好き|すき}だったのかしらね。
dialogue.en: Maybe that's why {隼人|はやと}さま loved soba too.
dialogue.note: 〜かしら: soft 'I wonder', used mostly by older women.

listening.intro: {恵子|けいこ}さん makes a plan for New Year's Eve. Type what she says.

lines.jp: {大晦日|おおみそか|New Year's Eve|3}も、ハナさんのそばを{食べよう|たべよう}ね。
lines.en: Let's eat ハナさん's soba on New Year's Eve too.

grammar.form: う-verbs: -u → -eば (まく → まけば, {飲|の}む → {飲|の}めば) · る-verbs: -る → れば ({食|た}べる → {食|た}べれば) · する → すれば · {来|く}る → {来|く}れば · い-adj: -い → ければ ({安|やす}い → {安|やす}ければ, いい → よければ) · negative: ない → なければ ({納|おさ}めなければ)
grammar.explanation: 〜ば states a condition: whenever A is true, B follows. It sounds general and logical, so it's perfect for rules, facts and advice. For a one-off event in the past ('when I got home…'), use たら instead.

examples.jp: {安ければ|やすければ}、{買います|かいます}。
examples.en: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

examples.jp: {分からなければ|わからなければ}、いつでも{聞いて|きいて}ね。
examples.en: If you don't understand, ask any time.

quiz.question: {毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}＿＿、{上手|じょうず}になりますよ。
quiz.en: If you practise every day, you'll get good.
quiz.explain: する is irregular: する → すれば.

quiz_more.question: {天気|てんき}が＿＿、{山|やま}に{行こう|いこう}。
quiz_more.en: If the weather's good, let's go to the mountains.
quiz_more.explain: いい conjugates from よい: よければ.

quiz_more.question: {年貢|ねんぐ|rice tax (Edo period)|2}を{納め|おさめ}＿＿、{罰|ばつ}を{受けた|うけた}。
quiz_more.en: If you didn't pay the rice tax, you were punished.
quiz_more.explain: ない works like an い-adjective: ない → なければ.

kanji.where: Handwritten on the paper bag of buckwheat flour ハナおばあちゃん brought.
kanji.breakdown: {十割|じゅうわり}: 十 ten + 割 tenths → 'ten tenths' of buckwheat: no wheat flour at all.
kanji.related: {二八|にはち}そば = 8 parts buckwheat, 2 parts wheat: the most common kind.

tip.title: Soba on New Year's Eve
tip.body: On {大晦日|おおみそか} most families eat {年越|としこ}しそば. Long noodles wish for a long life, and soba breaks easily, so it 'cuts off' the year's bad luck. Don't leave any in the bowl.

challenge.prompt: {恵子|けいこ}さん: 「アルちゃんも、そば{打ち|うち|making (noodles) by hand|2}やってみる？」 You answer that if you have time, you'd love to try. One part is wrong.

parts.why: ある is an う-verb: ある → あれば.

challenge.model_answer: {時間|じかん}があれば、ぜひやってみたいです！
challenge.explanation: ある changes its last sound -u to -e and adds ば: あれば, 'if I have'. ぜひ adds real enthusiasm, and やってみたい means 'I want to try'. です keeps it polite for {恵子|けいこ}さん.

vocab.note: な-adjective. 〜で{有名|ゆうめい} = famous for…
{土|ど} earth + {地|ち} ground. Also 'a region': {土地|とち}の{料理|りょうり} = local food.
Intransitive: plants and children grow. To raise = {育|そだ}てる.
{種|たね}をまく = sow seeds. Also 'cause': {心配|しんぱい}の{種|たね}.
Formal: {税金|ぜいきん}を{納|おさ}める = pay taxes.
{理由|りゆう}は〜からです = the reason is…
For a period already named. Casual: あの{頃|ころ}.
{長生|ながい}きする = live long. {長|なが}い + {生|い}きる.

kanji_study.parts: On top, an upside-down newborn child; below, 月 the 'flesh' radical (body) → a baby's body getting bigger: grow, raise.
正 'correct' + 攵 a hand holding a stick → making people do what's right: govern.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 故 (old; reason): 故 has 古 on the left, 政 has 正.

Poured into your leftover sauce at the end and drunk.
